summary: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists a Tyler County tower named Fred as gone; the name matches a small community, but no source found describes the tower's build, staff or site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as Tower Gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no later status found

evidence.supports: listed as Tower Gone in Tyler County at 30.56652, -94.19422
community seven miles south of Spurger in extreme southeastern Tyler County
evidence.quote: Fred is seven miles south of Spurger in extreme southeastern Tyler County.

evidence.supports: post office established 1881 with Wiley Cunningham as first postmaster
evidence.quote: The Fred post office was established in 1881 with Wiley Cunningham as the first postmaster.

evidence.supports: 1883 population thirty, two churches, general store, school
evidence.quote: In 1883 the community had a population of thirty, along with two churches, a general store, and a school.
The community's population had risen to seventy-five by 1913.
By the late 1960s Fred had 349 residents, and from the early 1970s through 2000 it reported a population of 239.

evidence.supports: post office one of three in Tyler County in the 1960s
evidence.quote: The Fred post office was one of only three post offices extant in Tyler County in the 1960s.

evidence.supports: new brick post office building opened 1976
evidence.quote: A new brick post office building opened in 1976, and was still operating in 2004.

sources.title: Fred, TX
sources.publisher: Handbook of Texas Online, Texas State Historical Association

notes_for_editor: The only lookout-specific source is the undated Forest Fire Lookout Association list, which gives a name, coordinates, type and Tower Gone status. Nothing read gives a build date, design, height, staffing, fire record or the reason it came down. The name matches the community of Fred (TSHA), but no source links the tower to the community, so the story does not say the tower was named for it. Two Portal to Texas History searches for Fred fire tower and Fred lookout gave nothing usable (the second returned 82 hits for the common name Fred, none checked). A Wikipedia coordinate for the community (30.57667, -94.17639) lies about 1.6 km from the list's point, but it was not quoted. The Kirby Forest tower in Tyler County (Tower Standing on the list) is a different site and is not connected to Fred. No photos added.
